about: Targets for tools/movement/measure.mjs, measured from the reference screen recording (3024x1898 retina, 60 fps, 12.86 s, 740 frames; one player rabbit on the keyboard, seated NPCs). Method and numbers: docs/study/art/movement-reference.md. 'ref' says where in the clip each number comes from (frame indices are 0-based decoded frames of the clip). A metric with "info": true is printed and compared but never fails the run. Tolerances come from the clip's own scatter plus one frame (16.7 ms) and one css pixel of measuring error; tighter than that is noise. Units: 'art px' are the sprite sheet's pixels; the reference draws 3 css px per art px, ours 4 on a 1512 px wide window (k in the harness header).

speed_hs_axis.ref: 269 css px/s = 89.7 art px/s over a sprite 40 art px tall; 17 held-key runs, idx 7-664
speed_hs_axis.note: Sprite heights a second. INFO, not gated: ours is coupled to the iPad's walk speed (LIVE_SPEED 70 art px/s, docs/study/library.md 'Walking'), so it may only change together with the wire's speed assumption. In css px a second ours (280 at k=4) is already the reference (269).

speed_hs_spread.ref: left 255-271, right 270-272, down 262-267, up 270 css px/s: max/min 1.04
speed_hs_spread.note: Same speed in all four directions (no extra perspective scaling).

speed_diag_ratio.ref: idx 66-70: 3 px per axis per frame = 254 css px/s against 269 straight
speed_diag_ratio.note: Diagonal about the same speed as straight (normalised), not 1.41 times. One 5-frame sample only.

start_delay_ms.ref: full speed within 2 frames at idx 29-32 and 55-58; no acceleration ramp
start_delay_ms.note: Effective delay of the fitted constant-speed line after the key goes down.

stop_excess_ms.ref: idx 50-52 and 664-666: -5, -3, 0 px; no coast, no overshoot, no settle
stop_excess_ms.note: How far past (+) or short of (-) the release the sprite travels, as milliseconds of walking.

stop_settle_ms.ref: motion ends within 1 to 2 frames of the last step (idx 50-52, 664-666)

display_update_hz.ref: the sprite moved on every one of the 60 recorded frames (2 recorded frames in 3 are not duplicates: 63 gaps of 25 ms are recorder drops)
display_update_hz.note: Distinct on-screen updates a second while walking (sprite, camera or pose changed).

pos_quantum_css.ref: native frame: sprite edges at device-px offsets 1, 3, 5 modulo the 6 px art pixel (idx 32-51): positioned at whole css pixels, 1/3 art pixel
pos_quantum_css.note: Smallest step the sprite can be placed at. Ours is a whole art pixel (k css px).

step_css.ref: 4.5 css px per frame at 60 Hz
step_css.note: Size of one visible jump. Judder amplitude: half of this per axis of the reference, double ours.

pose_rate_hz.ref: pose changes every 84.0 ms mean (13 slots idx 94-157: 75-92 ms, 5 recorded frames each = 12 Hz)

pose_dist_hs.ref: 269 px/s x 84.0 ms = 22.6 css px = 7.5 art px = 0.19 sprite heights per pose
pose_dist_hs.note: How far the body travels per pose. Larger means skating (the feet slide).

cycle_ms.ref: front view: 9 slots (B A C D E F E D A) = 0.75 s, 67 art px = 1.7 H
cycle_ms.note: With six drawn frames a cycle of 6 slots at 12 Hz is 500 ms; accepted.

distinct_poses.ref: A B C D E F (6 drawn poses, 3 of them used twice)

head_bob_rows.ref: head 1 art px (3 css px) higher in poses C and D than in A and E; no squash or stretch
head_bob_rows.note: Peak to peak head height over the walk frames of the sheet.

ground_shadow_w_hs.ref: purple ellipse 57 x 18 css px = 19 x 6 art px = 0.475 H wide, 0.15 H tall, fixed under the feet in every pose, also when standing
ground_shadow_w_hs.note: Width of the darkened patch the engine draws under a standing person, in sprite heights. 0 = none.

idle_changes_1250ms.ref: idx 668-739 (1.25 s standing): not one pixel changes
idle_changes_1250ms.note: Cannot say what the reference does after 1.25 s; ours animates the idle pose every 0.6 s.

cam_lag_steady_css.ref: while the camera scrolled (167 frames) the player's screen x stayed 756.7 +- 0.7 css px; the camera moved the same frame as the player (idx 225, 293, 328, 346)
cam_lag_steady_css.note: How far the player slides from his lock point while walking (distance behind).

cam_settle_ms.ref: camera stops the frame the player stops (idx 243, 312, 341, 357)
cam_settle_ms.note: Time after the release until the player is back within one art pixel of his lock point.

lock_off_y_pct.ref: head 395-405 css px, feet 481 of 949: 0.7% below centre
lock_off_y_pct.note: Ours deliberately sits 20% of the view lower than centre (the entrance is at the bottom, the library opens upward): a product choice, not a movement-feel matter.

diag_keeps_face.ref: idx 62-70: left face kept through the diagonal, front the frame the left key went

turn_latency_ms.ref: front face appears on the frame the horizontal motion ends (idx 71)
turn_latency_ms.note: From releasing the held key to showing the new facing.

wall_turns_and_stays.ref: idx 21-29: pressing into a chair turns the sprite to front and the player stays put, 8 frames

click_speed_ratio.ref: no click-to-walk in the clip (cursor never moves); informational: a click walk should be as fast as the keys

npc_speed_ratio.ref: no NPC walks in the clip; rule: everyone walks at the player's speed

npc_pose_rate_hz.ref: no NPC walks in the clip; rule: everyone cycles at the player's rate

zoo_speed_hs_max.ref: animals are 23 to 26 rows tall, so a fixed art speed is a different number of heights

sprite_vh_pct.ref: sprite 120 of 949 css px = 12.6% of the window height (40 of 316 art px)
sprite_vh_pct.note: How big the person is on the screen; our k = 4 gives 10.5%.
